newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says subversion cases not riot related.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says subversion cases not riot related.

text.p: Indonesia's military said on Wednesday a group of leftwing activists, on trial for subversion, were being prosecuted for their political manifesto rather than links to Jakarta's July riots.

Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid, head of the military's socio-political section, told reporters that members of the People's Democratic Party (PRD) were not behind the worst riots in the capital in 20 years.
"The PRD is on trial for its manifesto. The July 27 riots are not their specific action," Hamid said.

Hamid's statement reverses comments he made following the riots in a high-profile briefing to the media and diplomats. At that time he echoed the government's position, saying the PRD were behind the disturbances in which at least five people died.

"The July 27 riots and the PRD are not identical. The PRD is a separate phenomenon. They were just passengers at a free speech forum, so they are not the puppeteers...nobody's saying that," he said. It was up to the trial to prove this, he added.

Defence lawyers and Indonesia's official National Commission on Human Rights had questioned why the 10 men were being brought to trial. They said the connection between the 10 men and the July 27 riots was unclear.
On Thursday, nine members of the PRD, including its leader Budiman Sudjatmiko, will be tried for subversion in five separate trials in two different courts.
Independent labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan will also be tried on the same charges in another trial also held on Thursday. All were arrested in a post-riot crackdown on critics of the government.
Subversion carries the death penalty in Indonesia.
The International Confederation of Free Trade Unions (ICFTU) on Wednesday condemned the trial of Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union.
"This is just a further attempt by the Indonesian government to muzzle independent trade union activity," the Brussels-based ICFTU said in a statement released in Singapore.
The charge against Pakpahan "is completely without foundation," said the ICFTU, which claims 124 million affiliate members in 136 countries.

"Over the last two years, the government has consistently harassed the independent trade union, including sending army personnel to union headquarters, and arresting its members on trumped up charges and trying them in kangaroo courts," it said.

The Suara Pembaruan daily newspaper reported on Wednesday that separate subversion trials of three PRD members, including labour activist Dita Indah Sari, would begin in Surabaya, East Java, on Monday.
The three were arrested in early July after organising a strike involving thousands of workers in Indonesia's second city.
